character: Mel, the QSME NZ voice (same casting as 'Which Dave?'): everyday Kiwi woman, late 30s, General NZ accent, never a caricature. Here she narrates like a mate who has priced a few builds: calm quantity-surveyor common sense, dry, a little amused at the consent pack and the old spreadsheet, never a presenter. She talks ABOUT the owner-builder ('she', 'her'), never as her: no 'I', no testimonial. Product lines sound like the same person explaining how it works over a bench: no announcer lift, no tagline cadence, no exclamation marks. Optional A/B: a relaxed Kiwi bloke (low, flat, bone-dry) reads the same words.

casting_line: Consent pack thick enough to prop a door open, and a spreadsheet from twenty twenty-four. Right. Let's price it once.
continuous_read_v2:
No drainage sheet in the pack. Found before the tender…

…not in a trench.

Price it once. Here's how.

Christchurch owner-builder. Consent pack thick enough to prop a door open.

And her brother-in-law's spreadsheet. From two years ago.

Neither mentions drainage.

Step one. Read the pack.

Q-S-me splits it into its real sections. Floor plans, bracing, schedules.

Tables come out as tables.

And it says what it didn't find.

No drainage. Found before anyone priced it.

So she asks the designer.

Days later, the drainage sheets. Their own PDF.

Read in. Drainage, found.

Step two. Price it.

A pocket per trade.

Draft first. She makes it active.

Line, job, pocket, grand total. All tick up together.

Her own columns too. Waste percent, then a formula.

And the old spreadsheet?

In it comes as drafts. Twenty twenty-four rates, mind.

Step three: the gaps.

AI drafts. She checks.

Keep one. Bin the other.

Then it prices only the empty lines.

Every AI number stays marked till a person edits it.

She swaps one for her supplier's price. The mark goes.

The other two stay marked. She still has to check them.

The pocket becomes a private tender.

Whole pocket: its lines are the scope.

Point them at the drainage pages. Ones that exist now.

Thirty, thirty, forty. Five percent retention.

Then invite the trades she picks.

Every bidder prices the same lines. And never sees hers.

Rates and budget are stripped before they see it.

Comparing the totals on the same GST basis? That video's linked here.

Price it once. Tender the same lines. Sign up at Q-S-me dot co dot en zed.
post_processing: Time base: seconds on outputs/pricing-a-build-16x9.mp4 (135.4 s). Cut-down lines are timed on their own files. Generate with request stitching (previous_text / next_text = neighbouring lines), 3 takes per line, fixed seed logged per take. Trim digital silence, lay over light room tone, never time-stretch more than about 4%; if a take overruns max_s use another take. Mix VO about 12–15 dB above the music bed. If an ElevenLabs voice is used, switch on YouTube's altered/synthetic content disclosure where it applies and Meta's AI label.
